newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dehaene says Vilvoorde shows need for EU rules.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene says Vilvoorde shows need for EU rules.

text.p: French carmaker Renault's decision to close its plant near Brussels proves the European Union needs rules for cross-border company decisions, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday.

"The events at Renault Vilvoorde demonstrate the necessity of having at the European level a minimum of coordination in matters of employment and a minimum of common rules on social matters," he said at a ceremony to celebrate the 50th anniversary in Belgium of pipemaker Van Leeuwen Buizen.
Renault provoked a storm of protest in February with the shock decision to close Vilvoorde in July, costing 3,100 jobs.
France's newly-governing Socialist Party on Wednesday repeated campaign pledges to re-open the issue with the aim of getting Renault to reverse its decision.

Dehaene said there were texts on the table to create common rules on decisions by companies affecting employment across borders, but the EU needed to go further and make sure that decisions on such rules were not subject to national veto.
He said the EU's review of the Maastricht treaty, due to be concluded at a summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17, offered a prime opportunity to achieve this goal.
